newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest Sanevit to return to mkt in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest Sanevit to return to mkt in Feb.

text.p: The Bucharest bourse said on Friday it would lift a suspension of listed Sanevit in the early weeks of February after the company board had approved an asessment of equipment to be added to its capital.
"At this point there is no final figure for Sanevit's capital base and therefore trading cannot be resumed right now," said stock exchange general manager Stere Farmache.

Sanevit, Romania's sole producer of disposable syringes, was suspended last November pending a statement on a meeting of shareholders who decided to have imported equipment evaluated and added to its share capital of 24.7 billion lei.

The equipment -- bought from Italy's Penta Group on a $37 million credit guaranteed by the Romanian state -- was assessed by accountants Coopers and Lybrand, company general manager Mircea Roman said from the Transylvanian city of Arad.
He said the new size of Sanevit's capital would be released in February.
Shareholders also agreed on a 1997 output level of 125 million syringes and 390 million needles, Roman said. The domestic market can absorb up to 300 million syringes and 400 million needles a year.
Roman said shareholders also discussed a possible raising of $12 million from a direct placement to diversify output.
Sanevit had a six-month net profit of 518.9 million lei last year, up from 377.8 million in 1995, according to latest available data.
Before trading in Sanevit shares was halted, the company closed at 9,100 lei, compared with a 71,000 lei price when it joined the bourse in November 1995. ($= 5,932 lei)
